_readme: State for every community event the site promotes, and WHEN that state was
last checked against the organizer's own page.
This file exists because the site advertised $60/$45 early-bird pricing for
fifteen days after the early-bird tier disappeared from the organizer's page,
four days before the event. Nothing on the site knew the claim had an expiry.
tools/gate-events.mjs reads this. It FAILS the build when an event inside
seven days has not been re-verified within 24 hours, and when an event that
has finished still carries registration language. Bump statusVerifiedAt only
after actually re-fetching the organizer's page — a timestamp typed without a
fetch is worse than no timestamp.

events.name: Pickle for a Purpose
events.organizer: Echelon LA Metro — The Salvation Army
events.description: Echelon LA Metro's first annual charity pickleball tournament. Mixed doubles, beginner through advanced, organized in support of The Salvation Army's Los Angeles-area programs.

location.name: Peninsula Racquet Club
location.mapsQuery: Peninsula Racquet Club, 30850 Hawthorne Blvd, Rancho Palos Verdes, CA

events.verifiedBy: curl of sourceUrl; SportsEvent JSON-LD parsed from the response

note: Every offer reports SoldOut, down to a single $5 raffle ticket. That
reads like a closed ticket widget rather than a literal sell-out, and
only the organizer can tell those apart — so the site says
'registration is currently unavailable on the organizer's site' and
links out. It does NOT say sold out.
The $60/$45 early-bird tiers that were live on 2026-08-08 no longer
appear on their page in any form. Do not restore them.
Once endsAt passes, 'registration is currently unavailable' becomes a
different kind of wrong - it implies the event is still ahead. The page
moves to the 'ended' state: past tense, no registration CTA, no prices
presented as purchasable, no Offer nodes in the schema.
What is NOT required is a recap. Photos, results and a write-up belong to
the organizer, and a gate that stays red until one exists is a gate that
pressures somebody into inventing one. 'This event has taken place' is
complete and true on its own. Add a recap if and when there is real
material for it.
Three mechanisms, deliberately layered:
1. tools/build-event.mjs writes the ended state into the page, schema
and every CTA from this record. One command, no hand-editing.
2. An inline script in the page swaps to an ended banner the moment
endsAt passes, covering the hours between the event and the next
deploy. A seam cover, never the source of truth.
3. tools/gate-events.mjs fails the build while forward-looking copy
survives after endsAt - and says which command fixes it.

_note: Which states exist, and what each one is allowed to assert. The page
renders exactly one of them; tools/build-event.mjs picks it from
startsAt, endsAt and registrationState, then writes the status line, the
CTA labels, the pricing framing and the whole JSON-LD block from this
record - so those four can no longer disagree with each other.
The wording for each state is in tools/build-event.mjs (COPY). Facts live

note: Inside seven days of an event, a stale claim is expensive: someone may be
about to drive there. Outside that window the gate is quiet — it does not
nag about an event three months away.
